To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
molecular dynamics simulations of [Fe]- hydrogenase I from Clostriudium pasteurianun indicate that hydrogen diffuses more easily through the enzyme than oxygen.
molecular dynamics can be used to investigate O(2)-inactivation in [Fe]-hydogenase, and that the conserved active-site domain is essential for protecting the H-cluster from O(2) poisoning.

molecular dynamics simulations and experimental investigations of [Fe]-hydorgenases reveal that H(2), but not O(2), can diffuse freely to and from the enzyme's active site, suggesting that the protein structure plays a role in O(2)-inactivation of [FeS] hydrogenases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of protein conformation in H(2) production by [Fe]-hydrogeneses.
the role of protein architecture in the function of hydrogenase enzymes.
the role of protein environment in the catalytic activity of [Fe]- hydrogenases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
H(2)-diffusion is more favorable than O(2) -diffusion in CpI, and the protein structure plays a significant role in the diffusion of O(2).
the active site domain of CpI [Fe]-hydrogeanase provides the primary protection against O(2) inhibition, while the rest of the protein is responsible for facilitating substrate-product transfer.
O(2) is more likely to be excluded from the active site, than H(2) is to be allowed access to the active site.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the protein structure plays an important role in O(2)-inactivation of [Fe]hydrogenase.

O(2) access to the active site is restricted by the protein, while H(2) access is not, which is in agreement with the experimental observation that H(2), not O(2), is a substrate for [Fe]-hydrogenesis.
the conserved active domain acts to protect the active site by limiting O(2) access to it.
The main takeaway from our work is that
protein structure is an important determinant in O(2)-inactivation of [FeS]-hydrogenases.
the conserved active-site domain plays a key role in protecting the active site from inactivation by O(2), and that H(2)-diffusion in CpI is not limited by the conserved active domain.
molecular dynamics can be a useful tool to investigate the diffusion of substrates and products to the active site of hydrogenases.
